Q1: Should triage gain a cluster step?
Context:
- Today every crash report opens its own issue; nothing groups repeats (triage/intake.py:12).
- Upstream's cluster step computes a dedupe fingerprint, a SHA-1 hash (a fixed-length code computed from text, equal for equal text) of the report's first error line after addresses and line numbers are stripped, and attaches the report to the open cluster with the same fingerprint instead of opening an issue (vendor/upstream-triage/README.md:7-10).
- A cluster is upstream's group of reports that share one fingerprint (vendor/upstream-triage/README.md:8-10).
- The gap: one crash seen by many users shows up as many issues (vendor/upstream-triage/README.md:16).
My recommendation: yes, add the cluster step, keyed on upstream's fingerprint. It gains one issue per crash, at the cost of new grouping code in intake.
Basis: verified, vendor/upstream-triage/README.md:7-10 and triage/intake.py:12.
Alternatives:
- (a) Keep one issue per report. No new code, but duplicates keep hiding the crash count.
- (b) Group by exact error text. Simpler than normalizing, but addresses and line numbers split one crash into many groups (vendor/upstream-triage/README.md:7).
pass.why: defines every term it uses (cluster, SHA-1 hash), states upstream and today, and the recommendation and each alternative carry a gain and a cost
